parts.label: Part 1
parts.title: Jethro Tull (1674-1741)
parts.subtitle: Inventor of the Seed Drill The English gentleman farmer who revolutionised the practice of agriculture
parts.article:
Jethro Tull

A Jethro Tull was a major pioneer in the modernisation of agriculture. He was born in 1674 in Berkshire, southern England, into a family of land-owning gentry. He studied first at Oxford University and then at the Inns of Court, London, in preparation for a legal or political career. However, ill health caused him to postpone these plans, and after qualifying as a barrister in 1699, he made a tour of Europe, in the hope that the milder climates of France and Italy would alleviate his breathing problems. In every country through which he passed, he made careful observations of the soil and agricultural production, and on his return to England, the young Tull married, then began farming with his father at Howberry Farm in Oxfordshire.

B Tull was determined to improve farming methods and increase crop yield on the family land, and pursued a number of agricultural experiments there. He particularly wanted to increase efficiency in the sowing of seeds. At that time seeds were still thrown by hand across the field in a haphazard manner, in a traditional method known as broadcasting. Tull soon realised this method of random distribution was inefficient, being wasteful of both seed and labour, so he instructed his staff to sow seeds at very precise, low densities. But by 1701, his frustration with their lack of co-operation prompted him to invent a machine to do the work for him.

C Earlier in his life, Tull had once dismantled a pipe-organ, and the application of the technology behind this musical instrument inspired him to devise a drill that would distribute precise amounts of seed into pre-cut channels. Basic seeding devices had been known for almost 2000 years, but Tull took the concept a stage further. In his device, as the main wheels of the drill turned, the cylinder rotated against a spring-held tongue. This allowed seed to pass evenly from the hopper above to a funnel below. From here, the seed was directed at regular intervals into three channels, or furrows, in the earth. These were dug to a specific depth by the blades at the front of the machine. Spikes at the back of the machine then turned the soil over to immediately cover the seeds. Tull's 'seed drill' would limit the wastage of seed, and as the seedlings grew in uniform rows, it would also make it easier to remove any unwanted weeds growing among the crop. Accordingly, each plant would have more space to grow, and although there would be fewer plants, the net yield would be greater.

D Initially the machine was only a limited success, and in 1711 Tull decided to travel around Europe again, both to improve his health and to study agricultural techniques there. Upon his return in 1714, he perfected both his system and machinery. Following practices he had observed in the vine-growing methods of southern Europe, he used an animal-drawn hoe to turn over and pulverise the earth between the rows. He wrongly believed that this practice would release enough nutrients in the soil to nourish the crop, and so eliminate the need for manure to be used to fertilise the soil. His experiments were apparently successful, as he did manage to grow wheat in the same field for 13 successive years without the use of manure. However, it is more likely that it was the turning over and pulverisation of the soil that cut down on the volume of weeds competing with the seed.

E Tull's complete system eventually proved to be a major influence in the agricultural revolution, and its impact can still be seen in today's methods. Most subsequent drilling and hoeing implements have been either copies of, or improvements upon his inventions, and his modifications to the basic model of the plough continue to be visible in modern versions. Tull also advocated the use of horses over the oxen, more traditionally used to pull farm machinery, and published a book in 1731 outlining this and other ideas to enhance agricultural efficiency. The book caused great controversy when it appeared, and resistance to his revolutionary theories persisted for many decades. Another century would pass before his eventual vindication. It was only following the editing of his writings in 1822, and the subsequent translations and acceptance in France, that Tull's ideas finally achieved recognition in his native land. Although in his lifetime Tull's methods and inventions were dismissed and ridiculed, they were gradually adopted by large landowners, and in time, came to form the basis of modern agriculture.

analyses.content: 原文明确提到种子是从上面的“hopper”均匀地漏到下面的漏斗里，对应图表中位于上方的装种子容器。
你可能会根据常识想填入box之类的词，但题目要求必须用原文原词，且注意不要和下面的funnel填反了。
This allowed seed to pass evenly from the hopper above to a funnel below.
原文指出当主轮转动时，“cylinder”（圆柱体）也会随之转动，完美对应题目“turns as wheels move”的描述。
你可能会误填成spring-held tongue，但原文里真正发生转动（rotated）的是cylinder，tongue只是起支撑作用。
In his device, as the main wheels of the drill turned, the cylinder rotated against a spring-held tongue.
原文提到种子从上方容器向下进入“funnel”（漏斗），然后再进入渠道（channels），对应了图中连接上方容器和下方沟槽的部件。
你可能会看错图的指示方向而把hopper填在这里，一定要记住hopper在上方（above），funnel在下方（below）。
This allowed seed to pass evenly from the hopper above to a funnel below. From here, the seed was directed at regular intervals into three channels, or furrows, in the earth.
原文说到机器后方的“spikes”（尖状物）能翻动泥土来立刻覆盖种子，对应了题目“distribute earth over seeds”的功能描述以及图中标注在后方（Back）的部件。
你可能会因为不认识单词错填成前方的blades（用来挖坑的），要注意看图中标注此部件是在“Back”（后方）。
Spikes at the back of the machine then turned the soil over to immediately cover the seeds.

groups.contentHtml:
5. What name was given to the traditional technique of seed-sowing?
6. What type of agriculture gave Tull inspiration on his second tour of Europe?
7. What traditional addition to soil did Tull believe to be unnecessary?
8. What animals did Tull recommend farmers should use to pull their machinery?

analyses.content: 原文直接说明，以前人们随意撒种子的这种传统播种方法（traditional method）被称作（known as）“broadcasting”。
你可能会填入haphazard manner，但这只是描述播种方式很随意，并不是这种技术的专有名称。
At that time seeds were still thrown by hand across the field in a haphazard manner, in a traditional method known as broadcasting.
原文提到Tull第二次去欧洲游历时，观察并借鉴了南欧的“vine-growing”（葡萄种植）方法。
你可能会想填agricultural techniques，但这只是个大统称，题目问的是具体哪种类型的农业（What type of agriculture）给了他灵感。

Initially the machine was only a limited success, and in 1711 Tull decided to travel around Europe again, both to improve his health and to study agricultural techniques there. Upon his return in 1714, he perfected both his system and machinery. Following practices he had observed in the vine-growing methods of southern Europe, he used an animal-drawn hoe to turn over and pulverise the earth between the rows.
原文指出Tull错误地认为光靠松土就能释放足够养分，从而消除了对“manure”（粪肥）的需求，对应题目中问他认为什么是不必要的（unnecessary）。
你可能会填nutrients，但这是土壤里释放出来的养分，他认为不需要额外添加的传统物质是肥料（manure）。
He wrongly believed that this practice would release enough nutrients in the soil to nourish the crop, and so eliminate the need for manure to be used to fertilise the soil.
原文提到Tull提倡使用“horses”（马）来代替更传统的牛（oxen）去拉农用机械。
你可能会误填oxen，但原文说的是use of horses over the oxen（用马优于用牛），所以他推荐使用的是马。
Tull also advocated the use of horses over the oxen, more traditionally used to pull farm machinery, and published a book in 1731 outlining this and other ideas to enhance agricultural efficiency.

questions.question: Tull was employed in the legal profession before taking up farming.

analyses.content: 原文说他虽然学了法律且获得了律师资格，但因为健康原因推迟了计划（postpone these plans），去旅游后就直接开始务农了，并没有真正从事过法律工作。
你可能只看到他拿了律师资格（qualifying as a barrister）就着急选了TRUE，做判断题一定要看完整的句子发展，他因为生病并未上岗。

He studied first at Oxford University and then at the Inns of Court, London, in preparation for a legal or political career. However, ill health caused him to postpone these plans, and after qualifying as a barrister in 1699, he made a tour of Europe, in the hope that the milder climates of France and Italy would alleviate his breathing problems. In every country through which he passed, he made careful observations of the soil and agricultural production, and on his return to England, the young Tull married, then began farming with his father at Howberry Farm in Oxfordshire.

questions.question: The staff on Tull's farm were unwilling to follow his instructions.

analyses.content: 原文提到员工的不配合（their lack of co-operation）让他非常沮丧，这跟题目里的“不情愿听从指令（unwilling to follow his instructions）”是一个意思。
不要因为原文没有明明白白写出“unwilling”就选NOT GIVEN，lack of co-operation就是不情愿配合指令的完美同义替换。

Tull soon realised this method of random distribution was inefficient, being wasteful of both seed and labour, so he instructed his staff to sow seeds at very precise, low densities. But by 1701, his frustration with their lack of co-operation prompted him to invent a machine to do the work for him.

questions.question: Tull reduced the amount of weeds in his wheatfield.

analyses.content: 原文说他翻土的做法切实减少了杂草的数量（cut down on the volume of weeds），这直接对应了题目中的“reduced the amount of weeds”。
你可能会因为第23句只说了“小麦实验成功”没提杂草而误选NOT GIVEN，但真正的答案解释句其实在紧接着的第24句中。

His experiments were apparently successful, as he did manage to grow wheat in the same field for 13 successive years without the use of manure. However, it is more likely that it was the turning over and pulverisation of the soil that cut down on the volume of weeds competing with the seed.

questions.question: Tull lived to see his ideas finally accepted.

analyses.content: 原文第31句明确说到“在他有生之年（in his lifetime），他的方法和发明遭到了驳斥和嘲笑”，说明他活着的时候根本没有看到自己的想法被接受。
你可能看到前面说他的理论最终被认可（eventual vindication）就选了TRUE，但原文第29句明确强调了这是“过了一个世纪之后（Another century would pass）”的事情，那时候他早就不在人世了。

The book caused great controversy when it appeared, and resistance to his revolutionary theories persisted for many decades. Another century would pass before his eventual vindication. It was only following the editing of his writings in 1822, and the subsequent translations and acceptance in France, that Tull's ideas finally achieved recognition in his native land. Although in his lifetime Tull's methods and inventions were dismissed and ridiculed, they were gradually adopted by large landowners, and in time, came to form the basis of modern agriculture.

questions.question: Tull's original book, published in 1731, sold very few copies.

analyses.content: 原文确实提到他的书在1731年出版，也提到了这本书引起了巨大争议，但全篇上下根本没有提到过这本书的“销量（sold very few copies）”到底好不好。
你可能会自行脑补“既然有争议，那肯定没人买卖得不好”而选TRUE，或者觉得“有争议说明热度高，销量肯定好”选FALSE。雅思阅读切忌凭借主观常识脑补，没写就是没写。

Tull also advocated the use of horses over the oxen, more traditionally used to pull farm machinery, and published a book in 1731 outlining this and other ideas to enhance agricultural efficiency. The book caused great controversy when it appeared, and resistance to his revolutionary theories persisted for many decades.
